h.strategy: Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the main source of ideas: each hypothesis should exploit a specific open question or a default assumption that may fail under some parent condition. Aim for conditional effects that are non-obvious but mechanistically grounded: diminishing returns when a capacity is already present, substitution between alternative paths, edits that only matter when another part is a bottleneck, and reversals where a normally good edit becomes harmful. Cover a broad spread of edit fields, condition fields and both directions, with no duplicate rationales. State in each 'why' the mechanism and the observable result that would contradict it.

hyps.why: With edge 5 removed the direct skip is the main shortcut to the output, whereas it is redundant when the 2-hop path is intact.
Edge 0 none disconnects node 1 from the input so an edit on edge 4 is inert.
Replacing a skip loses the identity path, so the net gain is smaller than when replacing none or other weak ops.
A 1x1 to 3x3 upgrade is incremental compared with replacing none or pooling.
With edge 5 none, node 2 has no route to the output, so any edit on edge 1 is inert.
Replacing a strong 3x3 conv on the direct edge with a skip loses far more than replacing a weak op.
With edge 5 none, node 2 is dead so a conv upgrade on edge 2 cannot affect the output.
Filling an empty direct edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole new path, gaining more than upgrading an existing op.
Reconnecting node 1 to the input gains more than swapping an existing op for a skip, which is often a downgrade.
When the direct edge to the output is absent, a short skip path from node 1 is more valuable than when edge 3 already provides one.
